opportunities.name: Stablecoin Issuers Have an 18-Month Runway to a Hard Licensing Deadline
opportunities.problem: The GENIUS Act's licensing requirement takes effect January 18, 2027 — after which issuing a payment stablecoin in the US without a federal or state license becomes unlawful — while the OCC, FDIC and Treasury are still finalizing overlapping 2026 rulemakings (OCC proposed rule March 2, 2026; FDIC board-approved proposal April 7, 2026; Treasury's own section-3 comment window running to October 19, 2026). Issuers are tracking three regulators' moving drafts simultaneously with no single readiness checklist.
opportunities.target_customer: Compliance leads at mid-size stablecoin issuers and the banks/fintechs deciding whether to become permitted payment stablecoin issuers.
opportunities.proposed_product: GENIUS Act Readiness Tracker — a standing brief mapping each issuer’s applicable regulator (OCC/FDIC/Fed/NCUA/state) to that regulator’s current rule stage, reserve/redemption requirements, and the January 18, 2027 deadline.
why_now: The licensing prohibition takes effect January 18, 2027 — a fixed, dated deadline, not a soft target.

Three federal regulators issued their own proposed rules on overlapping but not identical timelines in 2026, and the comment window on Treasury’s own rule does not close until October 19, 2026 — the applicable rules are still moving inside the deadline year.
Trade coverage already frames compliance as an ongoing, always-on reserve/redemption “data integrity problem,” an operational shift most issuers have not built yet.
opportunities.status_reason: High-stakes, dated, multi-regulator deadline with strong willingness-to-pay precedent — issuers are already retaining specialist counsel. The constraint is acquisition: issuers are a small, identifiable population that likely needs direct outreach or a channel partnership rather than inbound content alone.

evidence.note: FDIC’s own press release on its GENIUS Act notice of proposed rulemaking.
The OCC’s own bulletin on its March 2, 2026 proposed rule for federal qualified payment stablecoin issuers.
A top-tier law firm publishing detailed implementation guidance — evidence issuers are already paying counsel to track this.
A law firm already productizing exactly this cross-regulator tracking function — direct competitive evidence.

opportunities.name: MiCA’s Grandfathering Window Just Closed — Unauthorized CASPs Have No Extension Left
opportunities.problem: The MiCA transitional (grandfathering) period ended across every EU member state on July 1, 2026, with no extension mechanism written into the regulation — after that date, any crypto-asset service provider without full MiCA authorization must stop serving EU clients immediately or face fines, suspension, or forced closure, while national competent authorities were still processing backlogged applications right up to the deadline.
opportunities.target_customer: Compliance officers and founders at crypto-asset service providers that did not complete MiCA authorization before July 1, 2026, or that are entering the EU market post-deadline.
opportunities.proposed_product: MiCA Post-Deadline Entry Brief — an ongoing tracker of which national competent authority has the shortest realistic authorization timeline post-deadline, plus a wind-down-vs-apply decision framework.
why_now: The absolute EU-wide deadline was July 1, 2026, and ESMA has told national authorities there is no extension mechanism and to treat late applications with caution.
Processing backlogs pushed several national authorities’ authorization timelines well past the formal 25–40 business day completeness-assessment window through the deadline period.
41 firms were authorized in December 2025 alone — the single largest month on record — showing a last-minute rush pattern that is repeating around the July 2026 hard deadline.
opportunities.status_reason: A genuinely hard, already-passed EU-wide deadline (unlike the GENIUS Act’s still-future date) makes urgency and pain scores high, with strong confirmation directly from ESMA. Automation is lower because tracking 27 national authorities’ real processing queues needs ongoing human research, not a one-time template.

evidence.note: ESMA’s own statement confirming the July 1, 2026 EU-wide end of the transitional period and instructing national authorities to treat late applications with caution.
ESMA’s own MiCA activity hub, corroborating the transition timeline and authorization framework.
A vendor already productizing MiCA deadline tracking — direct competitive evidence for the tracker angle.
A vendor already monetizing the exact post-deadline buy-vs-apply decision — confirms commercial demand for this decision framework.
